item.title: Barn Owl 0.14.0
item.description: - **Eight weeks in the Roost.** The Now view's Today card has a second side: the last eight weeks as a calendar of moons, bigger and brighter the more your owls worked; your busiest day, streak and main repository; and when your owls fly, by weekday and hour. Click a moon to see that day. It's all from the daily log Barn Owl already keeps; nothing new is tracked. - **Unused apps** are judged only by apps Spotlight has indexed. Without Spotlight's "last opened" date, an app opened every day could look as old as when it was installed, and be offered for the Trash. - **Clearing clipboard history** can't be undone by a save that was already on its way, and the history file is readable only by you. - **Claude Code's settings** are changed only over what was read: if Claude Code changes them in between, Barn Owl reads them again first. They're never briefly readable by others while written, turning answers off leaves a file without our hooks untouched, and only Barn Owl's own hook is ever removed. - **Menu bar colours** save and redraw once a colour drag pauses, not on every tick. - **Helpers:** "back" counts only the current batch, a twig goes once all its helpers are back, and helpers no longer count in "Done today". - **VoiceOver:** clipboard and search results, the clipboard's remove button, the Roost's rows and three icon-only buttons now say what they are and do. - Fixed: a full disk could crash a clean-up while it wrote its log; Relaunch quit even when the new copy didn't start; out-of-range plan numbers could crash.

item.title: Barn Owl 0.13.0
item.description: - **Mistral Vibe gets an owlet.** Vibe 3 sessions show what they're doing, from Vibe's own session store: thinking, running a command, editing, searching, on the web, waiting for its helpers, fixing after failed commands, paused for a rate limit, done after a long turn, and when it wants your OK or has a question, with the command or question itself. The owlet takes the session's title, and follows `/clear` into the new session. Vibe's owlets are ember. - A new Vibe shows up the moment it starts, not at the next look for processes. - **Agents that call other agents.** When an agent starts another (Claude Code running `vibe -p …` or `codex exec …` for a second opinion or a piece of work), the helper perches with its caller: on a twig that grows out of the caller's branch, named for its model and what it's doing ("Devstral Medium · Running a command"), under one label that says who asked and how many are working and back. Past five, the rest huddle as a flock with "+N". Picking the caller lists all its helpers in the inspector; the Now view shows "3 of 10 back" on the caller's row; the quick panel counts them in its line; and a helper that needs you says who it's working for. Helpers are shown even though they run from a script. A session that's waiting for its helpers stays on its branch, though its agent reports itself idle, and when the last one is back its twig says "all 6 back" for a while. - A Vibe owlet that has waited over a minute and a half for the model's answer says how long ("Thinking · 3 min"), so a long answer doesn't look like a hang. - Codex sessions are matched to their own log by the file each one has open, so several Codex runs in one folder, or in worktrees, no longer mix up their logs. - Other agents run for a single prompt (`vibe -p …`, `codex exec …`) count as scripted, like the Agent SDK's sessions, and are hidden unless you show scripted sessions. - **Plan limits say whose they are:** "Claude · 5 hours", "Codex Plus · week", in the quick panel, the Roost and the widget, with the plan where the agent names it. They no longer read as if they applied to every owlet.

item.title: Barn Owl 0.12.0
item.description: - **The Roost: your coding agents as owlets.** Claude Code (in a terminal, the Claude app's Code tab or the Agent SDK), Codex, Copilot CLI, OpenCode, Gemini CLI and a few others each get a pixel owlet that shows what it's doing: typing, searching, running a command, thinking, waiting for its helpers, stuck, napping, or waving when it needs you. Each agent has its own colour, and a session's helpers sit beside it. - **In the menu bar and the quick panel.** While agents work, a small owlet sits beside the owl, with a dot when one needs you. The quick panel shows every owlet on a branch in a little night scene, a card for the one that needs you with what it asks and an Answer button, one line for the rest, and your plan limits as moons. - **The Roost window.** **Now** shows what needs you as cards holding the actual question or command, with a countdown on a question; who's working, with their teams of helpers; what's done today; and who's napping. Beside it, today hour by hour, your plan limits, time by repository and a flight log. **Tree** puts every owlet on one pixel tree, a branch per repository, with nappers curled up in the hollow and finished ones asleep in the nest, under a sky that follows the time of day and the real moon (or one you pick in Settings → Agents). Pop the tree out into its own window and keep it on top. Open the Roost from the quick panel, by searching for "roost", or with `barnowl://roost`. - **Show and Answer take you there:** to the very Terminal or iTerm tab the session runs in (macOS asks once whether Barn Owl may control it), or the very chat in the Claude app. Right-click an owlet to open its project in your editor, Terminal or Finder, or to hide or mute it. - **The island at the notch.** When an agent needs you, gets stuck or finishes, a small island grows out of the notch (or hangs from the top of the screen). Hover to read the whole question or command. Choose Off, When One Needs You (the default) or While Agents Work in Settings → Agents. It stays away while you present or use an app full screen, doesn't ask about a session whose app is already in front, and leaves muted repositories alone. - **Answer Claude Code from the island,** off by default: Allow Once, Deny, Always Allow, or one of a question's options, without switching apps. Turning it on adds two hooks to `~/.claude/settings.json`, after showing you the exact change and saving a backup. Nothing is allowed without your click, Always Allow adds only the rule Claude Code itself suggests (shown with exactly what it covers), and the usual prompt takes over whenever Barn Owl isn't running, you're in that session's app, or ten minutes pass. - **Notifications** when an agent needs you, gets stuck after three failed commands in a row, or finishes a task that took a few minutes, but only when the island can't show it or you've been away. - **Plan limits:** Claude's and Codex's 5-hour and weekly windows, with a forecast and a note at 80% and when a window resets. Claude's come from the Claude app's own usage history, Codex's from its session logs. For Claude's reset times, turn on Settings → Agents → Reset times for Claude: Claude Code's status line passes them on, and still looks as it did. An old reading says "as of". Barn Owl never asks a server and never reads a login. - **Keep awake while an agent is working,** a new rule added the first time Barn Owl sees an agent: your Mac and its screen stay awake while one works and for five minutes after. A session waiting for you keeps it awake for five minutes only. With closed-lid mode on, a closed MacBook keeps running too. - **A desktop widget,** small or medium: the Roost under a glass dome, its sky following the time of day. If Barn Owl hasn't updated it for 20 minutes, it says "As of" with the time. - **Your week in the Roost.** From Friday afternoon to Sunday, after a week with at least an hour of agent work, the quick panel offers a recap card to copy, save or share. Repository names stay hidden unless you show them. - The setup guide has a new step for coding agents and the island. - **What Barn Owl reads:** the agents' own session files in `~/.claude` and `~/.codex`, and the Claude app's session records and usage history. It shows each session's title, state, folder and branch and, while one waits for you, the command, file or question. It never keeps your prompts or replies, never reads logins, and nothing leaves your Mac. macOS may ask once whether Barn Owl can see your Desktop or Documents folder, when an agent works in a project there. - **Turn features off in Settings → General → Features:** coding agents, clipboard history, the Nest, automatic presenter mode and disk space warnings. A feature that's off now doesn't run at all; before, the clipboard, the Nest and presenter mode still checked in the background. With coding agents off, Settings → Agents offers to remove Barn Owl's entries from Claude Code's settings. - When more than one rule holds and one of them keeps the screen on, the screen now stays on; before, the first rule in the list decided. The quick panel says "Screen on" or "Screen can sleep", and which rule. - A rule saved by a newer version of Barn Owl no longer makes an older one lose all your rules; it skips just that one. - On a small screen, the middle of the quick panel scrolls, so its footer stays in reach. - Barn Owl no longer looks over the whole menu bar every time a helper process starts or quits (browsers and test runs start many): only when an app that can have a menu bar icon does, and once per burst. Less CPU while you work. - The owl on the Perch no longer gets cut off by the menu bar.

item.title: Barn Owl 0.11.3
item.description: - **Closed-lid mode now works like Amphetamine's:** on battery, without an external display, and with no password or set-up, also on company-managed Macs. Barn Owl asks macOS's power manager directly not to sleep when the lid closes, only while keep awake is on. Locking the screen as the lid closes is now an option, off by default, as in Amphetamine. The old way (`pmset disablesleep` and a sudoers rule) is gone; if it left sleep disabled, Barn Owl turns it off, silently where it can. A leftover rule file is harmless; remove it with `sudo rm /private/etc/sudoers.d/barnowl` if you like.

item.title: Barn Owl 0.11.2
item.description: - **Closed-lid mode on company-managed Macs.** Some Macs' administrator settings ask for a password for every change of this kind, which overrides the rule Barn Owl adds, so it couldn't switch closed-lid mode off and the Mac stopped sleeping with the lid closed. Barn Owl now checks that switching really works without a password before turning it on, explains when it can't, stops retrying, and if sleep is ever left disabled, says so and offers to fix it.

item.title: Barn Owl 0.11.1
item.description: - **Fixes crashes at launch.** Moving the pointer over the owl made macOS throw an error each time (Barn Owl answered to the wrong names), which could leave it in a broken state and crash a moment later. - **Setup no longer takes over the pointer.** Finishing setup, and Refresh Pictures in Settings, used to drag every hidden icon into view and back to photograph it; now they show all icons for a moment instead, and nothing moves. - Barn Owl never borrows the pointer while you use it: an icon it brought out for you goes back once you pause, and moves it makes by itself wait without holding up the ones you ask for. - Closed-lid mode can no longer end up on after keep awake quickly starts and stops. - The "can't hide icons yet" alert only appears when you click the arrow, not out of nowhere. - Big copies (whole log files, 6K screenshots) no longer slow Barn Owl down: text over a megabyte isn't kept, images are scaled down, and history is saved in the background. - Dark Mode and presenter checks no longer freeze Barn Owl while macOS asks for permission or Control Center is busy. - Clicking the covered desktop no longer takes the keyboard from your app. - A clean-up that times out can't hang; "awake 0.2" means a minute, not forever; and a few rarer cases that could crash or loop are guarded.

item.title: Barn Owl 0.11.0
item.description: - Without Screen Recording, icons whose name shows their state ("Wi‑Fi, connected", "OneDrive · Syncing") no longer count as new icons each time it changes, so they stay where you put them. - Presenter mode no longer starts for apps that capture the screen all the time (DisplayLink, screen recorders), and the battery cutoff now lets the Mac sleep while presenting too. - Closing Search or the clipboard hands the keyboard back to the app you were in. - Updates found in the background say so in a notification instead of jumping in front of what you're typing, and a running keep-awake session carries on after the update. - A very long number in search ("awake 99999999999999999999") no longer crashes Barn Owl; sessions are capped at a year. - Turning clipboard history off clears it right away, on disk too. - **Closed-lid mode now follows keep awake,** like Amphetamine with Power Protect. Close the lid while keep awake is on and your Mac keeps running, with the screen locked (unless an external display is connected); otherwise it sleeps as usual. Before, it stayed on until you turned it off. Turning it on asks for your password once, to add a rule that lets your account run exactly `pmset -a disablesleep 1` and `pmset -a disablesleep 0` without a password; turning it off removes the rule. On a MacBook, the setup guide offers it as one of its choices. If you had it on, Barn Owl offers to set this up, or to turn it off. - Barn Owl no longer borrows your pointer while you're working. Icons it puts back in place, or shows because they changed, now wait until you pause, and an icon macOS won't let it keep in place (like Control Center's Display) is left alone instead of being dragged back every couple of minutes.

item.title: Barn Owl 0.10.2
item.description: - Closed-lid mode stays on through updates, and through restarts when Barn Owl opens at login, instead of switching off (and asking for your password in the middle of shutting down). Quitting Barn Owl still turns it off.

item.title: Barn Owl 0.10.1
item.description: - Lighter on your Mac: Barn Owl no longer hears every pointer movement unless you've turned on showing hidden icons by hovering or scrolling (that alone cost a few percent CPU whenever the mouse moved), and the Barn's map of the disk is let go two minutes after you close the Barn.

item.title: Barn Owl 0.10.0
item.description: - **A fresher look.** Floating panels share one Liquid Glass style with a touch of dusk, and the owl's lavender is the accent everywhere. The quick panel puts the owl and a big countdown first, has one row of time buttons and round Control Center–style toggles. Search groups commands and icons and shows what Return does. Toggles bounce, icons settle onto the Perch, the Nest glows as a file comes near, and the app icon is a layered Liquid Glass icon with dark and tinted versions. Sizes read the same everywhere. - Clearing clipboard history or the Nest asks first. New links: `barnowl://quick` and `barnowl://nest`. - **The Barn**, for disk space: a storage bar that adds up to the whole disk, and Tidy Up, sorted by how safe things are. Safe caches and build files go in one click; macOS installers, apps you haven't opened in six months, big old downloads and app caches are yours to pick, go to the Trash with Undo, and can be emptied from it on their own. Each clean-up is locked to its own folders, waits while its app or a build is running, and asks before anything that can't be undone. Explore draws a ring map of the disk with the biggest files by kind, Quick Look and a basket for the Trash. It warns when the disk is nearly full, and never cleans by itself. - Barn Owl no longer uses CPU while idle: closed panels are torn down and hidden owls stop.

item.title: Barn Owl 0.9.1
item.description: - The owl's speech bubble stays inside its window and no longer covers the text next to the owl: the step titles in setup, "Keep Awake" in the quick panel, or the edge of the Perch. - `barnowl awake 2h` keeps the Mac awake for two hours instead of indefinitely, and search reads "awake 2 h" as two hours. - `barnowl show` only shows hidden icons; it no longer hides them when they're already showing. - Overnight keep-awake schedules, such as weeknights 22:00–02:00, count from the night they start. - Turning presenter mode off during a screen share keeps it off until the share ends. - Changing displays while presenting no longer brings hidden icons back. - Quitting with closed-lid mode on also clears its setting. - Pinned images no longer come back empty after a restart. - The clipboard panel keeps the right entry selected when the list changes, and pastes into your app when opened from search or Settings. - One panel at a time: opening the quick panel, the clipboard, search or Settings closes the Perch (and the other way round), instead of leaving it open underneath. - The Nest's tab under the notch keeps up when you add, remove or clear files from the clipboard panel's Nest tab. - After a session stops for low battery, plugging in clears "Stopped: battery low" from the status. - When presenting ends, desktop icons you showed again by hand stay showing. - **Keep me available** pauses while the display may sleep, so the display can still sleep and your Mac can still lock.

item.title: Barn Owl 0.9.0
item.description: - **Hide Desktop** now covers the desktop with a picture of your wallpaper instead of restarting Finder, so icons come back exactly where they were and Finder windows stay open. - **Hidden Files** lets Finder quit properly before reopening it, so it keeps its windows and icon positions. - The quick panel no longer closes when Barn Owl moves icons, for example when you start presenting. - When presenting starts, the owl says "Incognito!" instead of "Wide awake!". - **The owl everywhere:** it reacts to the quick toggles, dresses for what's going on (a headset in calls, glasses at your desk, a blanket in closed-lid mode, coffee on long sessions), perks up when you plug in, perches on the Perch, peeks over the Nest's tab and waves files goodbye, follows search results, and covers its eyes when you copy a password. - **Menu bar owl:** its eyes follow your pointer, it winks on Option-click, wears shades while presenting, droops in a session's last minute, glances at icons that pop into view, and blinks awake with your Mac. - **Surprises:** good morning once a day, a livelier night owl, Halloween, New Year and birthday outfits, tonight's real moon in the sky, a throwable owl in About, and `barnowl hoot` in the Terminal. - **Owl personality** in Settings → Appearance: Lively, Calm or Still. - **A collection** in Settings → About: 38 owl moments to meet. - The docs say macOS 26 *and later*: Barn Owl runs on macOS 27 too.

item.title: Barn Owl 0.8.0
item.description: - Barn Owl can update itself. On the second launch it asks whether to check automatically (once a day), and it always asks before installing. Change that or check right away in Settings → General, or use the new button at the bottom of the quick panel. - The Homebrew cask is marked as updating itself, so `brew upgrade` leaves it alone. - Clicking an owl in Settings → Appearance now always switches its colours. Before, a click on the owl itself was sometimes ignored.
